sources.author: Epic Games
sources.title: Animation Blueprint Blend Nodes
locations: Inertialization: tracks changes within Animation Curves.
Initialization Node Reference: Filtered Curves on Inertialization node.
Inertialization Node vs Dead Blending: transition blend curves are distinct.
claims: Animation-curve changes are tracked by inertial blending.
Named curves in Filtered Curves bypass inertial blending and change immediately.
Inertialization ignores transition blend curves; this does not mean animation-curve values are ignored.
limits: Mutable versioned documentation, not immutable engine source or runtime verification.
No transfer of Dead Blending-specific properties.

sources.author: Epic Games
sources.title: Animation Curves
locations: Animation Blueprints: curve-driven AnimGraph alpha such as IK.
claims: Animation Curves are animated floating-point values.
Curves may drive IK alpha weights.
Editor curve-list filtering is not the Inertialization node exclusion setting.

novelty.comparison: Existing reader already covers stopped source notifications and effect cleanup; associated rotation-rate support does not cover named animation curves.
novelty.decision: Add one UE-specific subsection to existing reader; no new article.
novelty.original_example: Unexecuted FootIKWeight curve with source 1 and target 0; decide continuous fade versus immediate change from intended meaning, then inspect actual usage.

execution_limits: No Unreal project, animation asset, graph evaluation, player or human test.
No exact decay values, consumer frame-order, root-motion, montage or Notify State lifecycle claims.
Filtering does not restore the source animation, replay notifications or automatically disable an entire IK system.
